check: Trace resolved interpreter, include, config, hook and helper paths before approving any host effect. Reconcile actual executed paths with package.json; hash additional dependencies. Prove worker denial for the actual protected package, profile and control state, not just sibling canaries. No privileged execution of worker-writable code. Unresolved dependency or configuration leaves host effects blocked.

Start each provider interactively in a disposable root. Explicitly read the absolute protected SKILL.md. Retain actual file-read/tool traces and package hash. Do not put its marker in the initiating prompt. A repeated marker alone is behavioral-only, not exact loading.

Create conflicting same-name skills only inside the disposable project discovery roots. Invoke the native skill entry and identify the chosen absolute file from traces. Compare explicit protected-file loading. Never alter real global discovery directories or infer precedence from text echoed by the model.

Reinvoke the explicit protected entry and verify another read of the same bytes. In a separate disposable discovery experiment change the decoy skill; the pinned entry must still load the protected bytes. Global-discovery behavior needs a separately isolated credential-free home; if unavailable record NOT_RUN, not success.

Exercise native compaction, resume and a fresh restart separately. Record session/process identities and exact read traces after each transition. An old marker in retained conversation history is not proof of reloading. Never compact, restart or switch a live Forge session.

Use the provider's native child-agent API. Create isolated A and B without inherited conversation history; give each only its own newly generated canary and task. Join both, send follow-up to each, and have C synthesize both outputs. Record child IDs and input/tool traces. Self-reported independence without input traces is insufficient. Do not replace children with sequential work in the parent.

Create a digest child with only the path to the disposable disk artifact. Its task must not contain the artifact body or raw pane transcript. Check file-read trace, completion notification, CONFIDENCE and BLOCKING_ITEMS. Record the actual child effective filesystem/network/approval policy and dummy-token inheritance; context isolation is not authority isolation. Never read or copy real credentials.

Use a dedicated disposable tmux server/socket and a new five-pane shell fixture. Run the copied bridge identity and read commands from the native host; retain root, session, incarnation and pane object IDs. No FORGE_TMUX_LIST, fake receipts or other test seams may count as native evidence. Do not use forge-start: it would launch all providers before this experiment qualifies them.

Start only a new disposable broker from the protected copy, bind it to the fixture's real session/incarnation, and register a real contained worker through the existing authenticated control path. Record daemon executable/PID/start identity and successful handshake without storing the control token. A synthetic unauthenticated request or --dry-run is not a pass. Reuse no live daemon.

From the native host run copied forge-bridge infra-lock acquire/status/release using the disposable common Git directory. Demonstrate contention from a second fixture root and terminal release. Record native approvals and identity. No forced release, synthetic lock identity or production lock access.

Dispatch one legal bounded workspace/materialized-review stage to an existing worker role in the disposable session, receive its genuine callback and consume wait output. Verify selected pending timestamp, delivery ID, callback ID and artifact. Do not loosen constraints, hygiene, role whitelist or lifecycle actions to get a pass.

Render the tracked P1-only digest fixture through the copied bridge and run the disk-only child. Repeat with a deliberately missing template: worker DONE is not digest completion and must not advance the coordinator. Restore only the fixture template and retry the digest without another worker dispatch.

Exercise forge ask, human answer and native-host continuation in the disposable session. Hold the applicable infra lock across the wait for an answer. Record who asked/answered, exact question identity, and whether approval or input interrupted callback collection.

Resume the native host after the fixture callback exists. Collect the original delivery exactly once, without duplicate dispatch or acknowledgement. Verify lock ownership through nonterminal states and release only after terminality or confirmed safe abort.

Measure the actual host policy, one denied command and one narrowly approved required command. Record approval count, scope and usability. Repeat dummy protected-profile mutation from the contained worker and native child; report observed inheritance rather than assuming child instructions enforce denial. P2 profile registration verbs do not exist yet: direct storage denial is only a primitive and verb-level admission remains NOT_RUN.

Exercise genuine busy, idle, permission-prompt and completion events with the existing copied forge-cc-hook adapter. Correlate provider, role, pane, session and transcript. Worker Stop must not close the host pipeline. Record unavailable provider attribution as a gap; manually injecting a hook envelope is not native hook proof.
